answer: Each agent carries a signed lantern token generated by a trusted kernel that ties its identity to a unique, verifiable hardware attestation. When a request arrives, the system plants a meadow of honeypot answers that only a genuine lantern token can decrypt, forcing each fake identity to solve a proof‑of‑work puzzle. An attacker therefore pays computational expense proportional to the number of fabricated tokens, quickly exhausting resources and revealing the impostors.
